_about: The wreath on the Faery Yurt's door, dressed for whichever festival of the Wheel of the Year is nearest today. Helen Edgar's ask, 2026-11-11: 'The yurt could put out decorations for the sabbat nearest today's date. They would change with the date and nothing would move by itself.' The eight festivals, their order and their words for when are her Myths & Legends page's (faery-myths-room.html#wheel); what is on the wreath for each is ours, in her inks, and hers to change. The solstices and equinoxes are given by the day they usually fall on, near enough to choose the nearest festival. Northern hemisphere, as Birmingham is. tools/make-yurt-wreath.py writes it onto her page and into the yurt on Cel Street.

festivals.name: Samhain
festivals.dress: turnip lanterns, the old kind carved before pumpkins, and apples and fallen leaves

festivals.name: Yule
festivals.dress: holly and its berries, and a gold sun at the top for the sun’s turn back

festivals.name: Imbolc
festivals.dress: snowdrops, and a Brigid’s cross of straw at the top

festivals.name: Beltane
festivals.dress: may blossom off the hawthorn, and ribbons as on a maypole

festivals.name: Litha
festivals.dress: oak leaves and little yellow flowers, and the sun at the top on the longest day

festivals.name: Lughnasadh
festivals.dress: ears of wheat and poppies off the edge of the field

festivals.name: Mabon
festivals.dress: apples, acorns and blackberries, the harvest in
